subject.title: [Bug]: macOS app 'Launch at login' stops sticking / appears to turn itself off after app updates

question: Should the macOS app treat the user's Launch at login preference as durable intent that is re-applied after Sparkle updates, even when live launchd state temporarily disagrees?
rationale: Current code treats live launchd state as the UI source of truth; changing that can preserve user intent but may also override deliberate manual launchd changes, so this needs maintainer policy before a repair PR.

options.title: Persist and reconcile user intent
options.body: Store the user’s enabled preference separately from live launchd state and reapply/validate the app LaunchAgent after Sparkle replacement while exposing clear recovery if launchd rejects it.

options.title: Keep launchd as source of truth
options.body: Leave the toggle tied to live `launchctl` state and add diagnostics or a Fix button instead of silently re-enabling after updates.

options.title: Wait for live update proof first
options.body: Defer implementation until a packaged macOS update reproduction identifies whether the failure is Sparkle replacement timing, launchd bootstrap state, or UI state drift.

recommendation.title: Persist and reconcile user intent
recommendation.body: Store the user’s enabled preference separately from live launchd state and reapply/validate the app LaunchAgent after Sparkle replacement while exposing clear recovery if launchd rejects it.

likelyOwner.reason: The history ties this person to the app LaunchAgent introduction and adjacent macOS config diagnostics, making them the best available routing owner for the source-of-truth decision.
